subject: Culture
title: Sanctuary and Asylum
description: A quick, practical guide to Sanctuary and Asylum.

hook.text: A medieval murderer who reached a church doorknob before the mob caught him was legally untouchable for 40 days.

buildup.text: Church sanctuary dates to Roman temples where fugitives could claim divine protection from secular law.

discovery.text: This tradition shaped modern asylum law. The 1951 Refugee Convention echoes the idea of sacred safe harbor.

twist.text: In 2007 an American church sheltered an undocumented immigrant for a year. The tradition still lives.

climax.text: Sanctuary cities directly descend from medieval churches declaring they answered to God, not the state.

punchline.text: The line between law and mercy is always contested.

quiz.question: How long could a fugitive claim church sanctuary in medieval England?
